turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to use them on Owen. A zero went into the gradebook, and he found out about it on his phone in the middle of class. Who decided that, and why didn't anyone call me first?
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
You reread them. That doesn't answer who decided on the zero, and I'm writing down that you skipped it. What did you find in them, specifically?
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. That's an impression, not a document. Who decided on the zero?
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why is there a zero next to his name? Thoughtful kids don't get that without a conversation first. I'm still waiting for an answer, Hale.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
It only becomes a fight when a zero goes in before anyone picks up a phone. Caring about him means that mark comes off today. Are you going to answer me, Hale, or keep telling me how we feel?
